text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: increased 5xx errors and high tail latency for inference endpoints in us-east-1a. Alert group: inference-frontend-us-east-1a.

pagerduty: SEV2 - 5xx spike >= 5% over 3m, latency p99 > 2s. Paging current oncall: @sre-oncall.

mira: seeing the same in dashboards — p50 up, p95 and p99 jumping. errors are mostly 502/504 from proxy layer.

ashok: graphs: outbound packet drops from instances in us-east-1a + resolver error counts spiking. Not all AZs.

samir: I can reproduce tail with curl to our health endpoint via an instance in us-east-1a — intermittent socket timeouts.

chris: starting to collect tcpdump from a healthy and affected host. placing on /tmp and uploading to s3. command: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/sniff.pcap port 443`

elaine: ENI attach/detach flaps? I see host-level kernel rx queues backpressure on the instance metric. Could be NIC saturation or driver.

eng-platform: Confirmed: some hosts in the AZ show rx_queue drops and increased retries to the resolver (169.254.x.x). AWS console shows no full AZ outage, but spotty network errors.

mira: mitigation plan: 1) route new traffic away from us-east-1a where possible 2) enable retry+shorter backoff in frontend for current requests 3) enable fallback model variant with smaller KV cache to reduce memory pressure.

sre-oncall: doing (1) now — updating smart-routing policy to prefer us-east-1b then us-west-2 for inference calls for non-data-residency customers. This will respect sticky sessions for pinned customers.

ashok: rolling policy change: `PATCH /routing/policy` with `prefer: [us-east-1b, us-west-2]`, live in 30s. Watch for increased cross-region latency.

samir: enabling retries in the frontend: `RETRY=3 BACKOFF_MS=150` for gateway to model service. Doing a quick canary on 5% of traffic.

elaine: moving some dedicated pools off of affected hosts. Initiating `node-drain` on three flagged hosts in us-east-1a to evacuate model containers.

chris: draining causes some cold-start latency for large models. to limit customer impact, we'll route in parallel to warm hosts in other AZs, not do mass drains at once.

incident-bot: Note: draining node i-0abc123 triggered model restart on two replicas; no data loss, only increased latency for in-flight sessions.

mira: customer-ops, get me an estimate of impacted customers and percentage errors. We should prepare a status page update if >5% customers impacted.

customer-ops: pulling from logs now — preliminary: ~12 customers saw elevated error rates; overall traffic affected ~6% of production inference calls from us-east-1.

ashok: starting a targeted reroute for customers with SLA tier Bronze and below first, to limit churn for enterprise customers pinned to AZ.

samir: also turning on prefix caching (short TTL) on the gateway to reduce repeated resolver lookups for hot KV keys. That should reduce resolver load.

elaine: opened AWS support case #123456789 — provided pcap and instance diagnostics. AWS SRE says they see anomalies in the AZ network plane and are investigating.

chris: log snippet from proxy: ```
[2026-03-15T01:05:12Z] proxy.go:504 error=timeout backend=us-east-1a/model-34 attempt=2
[2026-03-15T01:05:12Z] proxy.go:512 upstream_err=ECONNRESET
```

mira: can we enable our graceful degradation? For some routes we can return cached embeddings or degrade to 1/2 token generation length to reduce compute.

eng-platform: enabling degrade flag for low-priority routes now. `featureflag: inference.degrade_on_az_err = true`

sre-oncall: declaring SEV2 and adding @chris as incident lead, @mira as mitigation lead. Will prepare an incident timeline.

samir: I pushed a temporary LB change to shift 70% of new connections away from us-east-1a. Monitoring for errors/latency impact on other AZs.

incident-bot: Action log recorded: routing-change, retries-enabled, node-drain-initiated, aws-support-case-open.

mira: quick customer msg draft: "We’re investigating increased errors from us-east-1a impacting inference requests. We’ve routed traffic away from the affected AZ and implemented retries and degradations to reduce errors. We’ll update in 30 minutes." Approve? :+1: / :eyes:

customer-ops: approved. Posting to status page now. link: https://status.redwood.inference/incident/2026-03-15-us-east-1a

ashok: monitoring shows error rate dropped from 5.5% to 1.2% after reroute + retries. p99 latency still elevated for a subset of sessions that remained on the AZ.

chris: packet captures show resolver timeouts correlated with spikes. root cause hypothesis: noisy resolver or local NAT gateway retransmits causing connection resets.

eng-platform: as a temporary measure, we've added an iptables rule to prioritize DNS responses and bumped resolver timeouts in our host config. Not ideal long-term.

mira: next steps: 1) continue to steer traffic until AWS confirms fix 2) collect full host diagnostics and upload to infra S3 3) postmortem owner @elaine 4) customer follow-up email draft after incident closes.

elaine: taking postmortem. timeline assigned, will include why our AZ-fallback policy didn’t fully protect some pinned enterprise customers and action items to improve cross-AZ capacity checks.

sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall @chris in 20m — will summarize runbook and current mitigations in #oncall-handoff. If error rate creeps back above 2%, escalate to SEV1.

chris: noted. I'll keep watch and maintain the routing steer until AWS confirms. Thanks all — please add any logs or annotations to the incident thread. :wave:
